# Executive Summary

This report stages the EuRoC snippet material used for the compact TAES experiment assets. It summarizes the endpoint, runtime, and interpolation evidence behind the paper-side figure and tables.

Main conclusions:

- I used the same eleven aggressive EuRoC snippets as the PsyChMagPI gyro report, with smooth Chebyshev2 vector proxies fitted on 1 s windows and measurements restricted to the center 200 ms interval.
- For `M` samples, PsyChMagPI used the paper's advocated rule `m=M-1`, `n=floor(2*sqrt(m))`, and `N=n+1`; the five sample counts therefore used `N=[7, 9, 11, 13, 15]`.
- With no added noise, PsyChMagPI beat D3 single-speed in 80% of matched trials, with median endpoint error 3.05e-04 degrees versus D3's 0.001263 degrees.
- For final endpoint integration, PsyChMagPI used the historical approximate `N -> N` integration matrix and beat D3 single-speed in 45% of matched trials, with median final SO(3) error 0.1637 degrees versus D3's 0.1619 degrees.
- D3 single-speed was included as the classical coning baseline beyond D2/RK2, so the endpoint comparison is now aligned with the TAES draft's classical-method vocabulary.
- In wrapped GTSAM timing, D3 was 0.9x the runtime of D2/RK2, while PsyChMagPI was 34.3x the runtime of D2/RK2.
- I evaluated all interpolation evidence already developed for the EuRoC proxy study: gyro interpolation error, dense attitude trajectory error, and random-subinterval rotation error.
- PsyChMagPI had the best median gyro NRMSE, 0.1085. The best median trajectory RMS was `RK2` at 0.1374 degrees; PsyChMagPI had 0.1386 degrees. The best median random-subinterval RMS was `RK2` at 0.1244 degrees; PsyChMagPI had 0.1278 degrees.

# EuRoC Snippet Construction

I used selected EuRoC windows only to define smooth aggressive gyro proxies, not as ground-truth attitude trajectories. Each snippet is a 1 s bias-corrected gyro window fitted by a Chebyshev2 vector proxy with `N=50`; every endpoint and interpolation metric below uses only the shaded 200 ms center interval.

![EuRoC aggressive snippet overview.](taes_euroc_snippet_experiment_assets/snippet_overview.png){width=100%}

The proxy preview below shows the three bias-corrected gyro components and the smooth 1 s vector fit. This figure is useful for paper figure selection because it exposes both the raw IMU contamination and the smooth proxy used for controlled Monte Carlo evaluation.

![Raw bias-corrected gyro samples and Chebyshev2 vector proxies.](taes_euroc_snippet_experiment_assets/proxy_gyro_previews.png){width=100%}

# Final Integration on the Middle 200 ms Window

I compared final rotation accuracy on identical noisy samples using D2/RK2, D3 single-speed, and PsyChMagPI with the paper's polynomial-degree rule: for `M` samples and `m=M-1` intervals, `n=floor(2*sqrt(m))` and `N=n+1` CGL nodes. D2/RK2 composes trapezoidal per-sample Lie increments; D3 adds the adjacent-increment single-speed coning correction; PsyChMagPI fits a global CGL representation before SO(3) integration and uses the historical approximate `N -> N` integration matrix.

![Endpoint median final attitude error.](taes_euroc_snippet_experiment_assets/endpoint_median_error.png){width=100%}

For snippet `i`, the component noise standard deviation is `sigma_i = alpha * range_t ||omega_i*(t)||`. Because that physical scale varies by snippet, the table lists the exact dimensionless `alpha` used by the experiment rather than a single rad/s value. The converged PS-CPI column uses the historical approximate `N -> N` integration matrix.

The per-snippet view checks whether the aggregate result is dominated by one EuRoC sequence. I aggregated across all sample counts, noise levels, and seeds for each selected snippet.

## Significance for Paper Table V

Boldface is restricted to lower medians with Holm-adjusted `p < 0.05`. Exact two-sided paired permutation tests compare pooled medians using all 2^11 snippet-level label swaps; all seeds, sample counts, and noise fractions within a snippet move together. This does not count duplicate no-noise seeds as independent snippets. Holm correction includes twelve tests: One-Speed versus PS-CPI and both angular-rate interpolation baselines versus PS-CPI, in each of four noise groups. PS-CPI interpolation is bold only if it beats both baselines significantly. These tests use the existing multi-rate caches, not the new fixed-rate Table IV cache.

| noise_group | metric   | baseline        | p_value   | p_holm  |
| ----------- | -------- | --------------- | --------- | ------- |
| none        | endpoint | D3 single-speed | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| none        | signal   | Linear          | 0.001953  | 0.01172 |
| none        | signal   | Cubic spline    | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| low         | endpoint | D3 single-speed | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| low         | signal   | Linear          | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| low         | signal   | Cubic spline    | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| mid         | endpoint | D3 single-speed | 0.001953  | 0.01172 |
| mid         | signal   | Linear          | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| mid         | signal   | Cubic spline    | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| high        | endpoint | D3 single-speed | 0.09961   | 0.09961 |
| high        | signal   | Linear          | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |
| high        | signal   | Cubic spline    | 0.0009766 | 0.01172 |

The new 200 Hz endpoint cache contains 36,300 rows (33 cells of 1,100 trials), with all 12,100 PS-CPI runs converged. `endpoint_200hz_provenance.json` records the py312 private-wrapper and library paths and hashes, source-data hashes, and experiment settings. The private wrapper was built in an isolated directory without replacing the default installed wrapper.

# Runtime Comparison

I timed the endpoint methods to estimate the computational cost that would accompany the accuracy results. This is a Python-level wall-clock benchmark of wrapped GTSAM calls, not a final optimized C++ timing claim: D2/RK2 calls `gtsam.integrateSequentialRotations`, D3 calls `gtsam.integrateSingleSpeedConing`, and PsyChMagPI calls the current GTSAM PsyChMagPI wrapper path using the historical approximate `N -> N` integration matrix and including the sample-to-CGL fit used by the report.

The benchmark used all eleven snippets, all sample counts, representative low/mid/high noise levels, and 5 deterministic noisy draws per snippet/sample/noise combination. Each row timed one final-rotation integration on the middle 200 ms window.

# Interpolation and Continuous-Trajectory Results

I included all three interpolation checks because the TAES paper can use them to separate endpoint integration accuracy from continuous representation quality. The signal methods are componentwise linear interpolation, componentwise natural cubic interpolation, and PsyChMagPI; the trajectory checks also include RK2 and Magnus-2 sample-trajectory baselines. PsyChMagPI uses the same paper rule `n=floor(2*sqrt(M-1))`, `N=n+1` as the endpoint experiment. Each table explicitly separates no-noise trials from positive low-noise trials and reports the strongest non-PS baseline beside PsyChMagPI.

To measure signal fidelity, I compared each continuous angular-velocity estimate against the clean Chebyshev2 proxy on a dense 1001-point grid.

![Gyro interpolation normalized RMSE.](taes_euroc_snippet_experiment_assets/interpolation_signal_nrmse.png){width=100%}

Gyro interpolation summary:

| Noise | Best non-PS  | Non-PS NRMSE | PsyCh NRMSE | PsyCh denoise dB |
| ----- | ------------ | ------------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| none  | Cubic spline | 1.97e-04     | 0.004287    | 0.00e+00         |
| low   | Linear       | 0.07064      | 0.04912     | 4.215            |
| mid   | Linear       | 0.1539       | 0.1085      | 4.345            |
| high  | Linear       | 0.2803       | 0.1959      | 4.362            |

To measure dense attitude fidelity, I integrated each continuous gyro representation over the dense grid and compared the full attitude path against the clean reference trajectory.

# Output Files

I wrote the paper-staging assets under `taes_euroc_snippet_experiment_assets`. The multi-rate endpoint trial rows are in `endpoint_trial_metrics.csv.gz`; the 41-sample Table IV rows are in `endpoint_200hz_trial_metrics.csv.gz`, with settings and binary hashes in `endpoint_200hz_provenance.json`. Runtime rows are in `runtime_trial_metrics.csv`, and interpolation trial rows and summaries are copied into the same asset directory so the paper figures can be regenerated without depending on the earlier report directory. Call `write_report_from_cache()` to refresh this QMD without executing experiments; generate missing 200 Hz trials explicitly with `run_taes_euroc_200hz_endpoint.py`.
